result.what_interviewer_wanted: Explain why a mutable default argument is dangerous in Python and how to avoid the pitfall.
result.improved_answer: A mutable default, like an empty list, is evaluated once at function definition, so every call shares the same list. If the function mutates it, data from previous calls leaks into later ones. The safe pattern is to use None as the default and create a new list inside the function. I ran into this during my internship when a helper that collected log lines kept growing across requests until I switched to the None‑pattern.
